claims.claim: In Dindorf vol. II the scholia on Od. 10.82–86 run from p. 452, line 25, to p. 454, line 18. Sigla: B (85), H, H.Q., H.V., T, P (86).
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 452 OCR: the lemma '82. τηλέπυλον] μεγάλην …' carries the line marker 20, and 'Λαιστρυγονίην]' carries 25. The P scholion ends at 454.18; '87. ἔνθ᾽ ἐπεὶ' follows. The sigla are correct.
claims.fix: The scholia on v. 82 begin at II 452.20 (τηλέπυλον), so write 'p. 452, line 20, to p. 454, line 18'.

claims.claim: The Crates note in H.Q. continues 'ἢ τὸν ἐν ὕπνῳ τὸ τῆς ἡμέρας πολὺ καταχρώμενον. H.Q.'
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 453.27–28. The OCR is garbled but consistent ('τον εν UVTyO TO τῆς ηβμέρᾶς πόλυ Κατ’ χρομε ον').

claims.claim: Two distinct Crates versions in the scholia: H.Q. 'περὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ δράκοντος' and H.V. 'κατὰ τὴν τοῦ δράκοντος αὐτοὺς κατηστερίσθαι κεφαλήν … ὡς ἀνάπαλιν παρὰ τοῖς Κιμμερίοις'; both quote Aratus 61–62.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 453.20–28 and 454.3–8 (OCR).

claims.claim: Dindorf prints νείσεται in both quotations of Aratus 61; Mair's Loeb prints νίσσεται.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 453.22 and 454.5 (OCR); Perseus Mair, Aratus line 61. Note also that Manitius' Hipparchus (p. 34) prints νείσσεται, with apparatus 'τῇ νείσεται LP²M'.

claims.claim: Dindorf's apparatus on 453.21: 'Ἄρατος] 61. ubi Cratetis sententiam memorat scholiasta'.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 453, apparatus line 21 (OCR '2T. "Apzros) 61. ubi Cratetis sententiam memorat scholiasta').

claims.claim: Dindorf supplied νυκτός, πολέμιος, βόσκων, illegible in B (schol. 10.85), from 'annotatio similis Eustathii p. 1648, 42'.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 453, apparatus line 8: 'Tria haec vocabula obliterata in B. supplevi ex annotatione simili Eustathii p. 1648, 42.'

claims.claim: Eustathius p. 1648 (Rome), c. lines 41–43: βουκόλους νύκτωρ νέμειν διὰ τὸν … πολέμιον οἶστρον … τοὺς δὲ ποιμένας βόσκειν ἡμέρας οὔσης.
claims.evidence: Stallbaum I 368. The passage lies between the Rome markers 40 and 50 of p. 1648.

claims.claim: Dindorf's preface says B (Ambros. B 99 sup.) contains material inserted from Eustathius by an interpolator; the B scholion on 10.85 may depend on Eustathius.
claims.evidence: Dindorf I praef. pp. xii–xiii: '…quae passim ex Eustathio inseruit interpolator (vide ad … κ 20. 153. 242. 251. 491 …)'. The 10.85 note is not listed, so dependence on Eustathius is only an inference.

claims.evidence: Dindorf II 453 apparatus '1. νομέα Buttm. pro νομός', '19. τῶν Buttm. pro τοῖς'; 454 apparatus '13. τὴν γὰρ νύκτα addidit Buttm.'

claims.claim: The H.V. scholion: Laestrygonians held the territory of Leontini, where gadfly and oestrus breed, so shaggy animals graze by day and smooth ones by night. Eustathius repeats this at 1649.10–19.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 453.29–454.3. In Stallbaum I 368 Eustathius has 'κατεσχηκότες τὴν περὶ Σικελίαν χώραν τῶν Λεοντίνων, ἐν ᾗ πολὺς ὁ μύωψ· ὥστε τὰ μὲν λάσια ἡμέρας … τὰ δὲ ψιλὰ νυκτός', between the Rome markers 1649.10 and 1649.20.

claims.claim: A scholion in H on 10.82 says the νεώτεροι identify Laestrygonia with Sicily.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 452.26–27: 'τὴν Λαιστρυγονίην οἱ νεώτεροι Σικελίαν φασί. H.'

claims.claim: The P scholion (23-hour day) closely paraphrases Geminus 6.10–12.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 454.12–18 ('κγʹ ὡρῶν', 'μιᾶς ὥρας', 'περὶ τούτων καὶ Ὅμηρος τῶν τόπων μνημονεύει') against Manitius p. 72. This is a parallel only; direct dependence is unproven, as the draft says.

claims.claim: Geminus 6.10–12 (Manitius p. 72) reports Crates 'the grammarian': 23 equinoctial hours of day, one hour of night.
claims.evidence: Manitius p. 72.2–20: 'Κράτης δὲ ὁ γραμματικός φησι … ὡρῶν κγʹ ἰσημερινῶν ἡ νὺξ … ὥρας μιᾶς'.

claims.claim: Herodicus (F 13 Broggiato = Athen. 5.192a–b) ironically cites Od. 10.84 about Socrates leaving the Symposium for the Lyceum.

claims.fix: Drop the inference about Pontani's sigla, or check his conspectus siglorum (vol. V pp. xxvii ff.).

claims.claim: No printed translation of the Odyssey scholia on 10.85–86 as such was found.
claims.evidence: A negative result. Bilić (TAPA 2012; Land of the Solstices 2021) very probably translates the Cratetean scholia into English, and Cullhed–Olson translate Eustathius' paraphrase. I did not check either.
claims.fix: Write 'no complete translation found; partial English renderings likely in Bilić 2012/2021'.

claims.claim: The lemma of the N scholion on 10.84 is ἄοκνος, with 'γρ. ἄυπνος'.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 453.7: '84. ἄοκνος] γρ. ἄυπνος. N.'

claims.claim: Kidd's 1997 text of Aratus 61 reads νείσεται.
claims.evidence: Kidd was not accessible. Mair prints νίσσεται; Manitius (Hipparchus) prints νείσσεται.

claims.claim: Allen's OCT text of Od. 10.80–86 is identical to Murray's.
claims.evidence: Allen was not consulted.

claims.claim: Crates' Laestrygonian testimony is fr. 50 Broggiato 2001 (Gem. 6.10–12; schol. Od. 10.86; schol. Arat. 62).
claims.evidence: Broggiato 2014 p. 106 n. 126.

claims.claim: In Broggiato's FGrHist V (Jacoby Online) edition the same testimony is 2113 F 20; not to be confused with Broggiato 2001 F 20 (Il. 14.246a).
claims.evidence: Bilić, GRBS 60 (2020) n. 10: 'Crates fr.50 Broggiato = BNJ 2113 F 20'. In Nagy's Harvard Continuum essay, Crates F 20 Broggiato is Plut. De facie 938d quoting Il. 14.246a. The Jacoby Online entry itself was not seen.

claims.claim: Mette 1936 numbers the Laestrygonian cluster fr. 37a–i (Σ HQ = 37e, Σ HV = 37f, Eust. = 37g, Σ Arat. 62 = 37h, Hyg. Astr. 4.3 = 37i, Σ P = 37d, Priscianus Lydus = 37b, Gem. 6.16–20 = 37a).
claims.evidence: Neither Mette nor Bilić 2021 was accessible. The only independent trace is Bilić 2020 n. 7: 'Crates fr.37b Mette (… 268.5-7)', in a Thule/arctic-circle context, which fits but does not prove 37b = Priscianus.

claims.claim: Geminus 6.10–12 attributes to Crates: a 23-hour longest day, a one-hour night, sunset next to sunrise; the cause is 'mathematical and consonant with the sphaeric theory'.
claims.evidence: Manitius p. 72: 'εἶτα ἐπιφέρει τὴν αἰτίαν μαθηματικὴν οὖσαν καὶ σύμφωνον τῷ σφαιρικῷ λόγῳ … ὅτι ἡ δύσις παράκειται τῇ ἀνατολῇ'. Shchetnikov, ΣΧΟΛΗ 5.2, pp. 197–198.

claims.claim: The 'head of Draco + Aratus 61–62' argument is preserved only in the scholia (Σ HQ, Σ HV, schol. Arat. 62), not in Geminus.
claims.evidence: Correct for Geminus. But Eustathius 1649 (Stallbaum I 369) also preserves it ('ὑπὸ τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ δράκοντος … ἣν καὶ Ἄρατος …'), probably drawing on the scholia.
claims.fix: Add 'and in Eustathius ad loc. (p. 1649 Rom.), who depends on the scholia'.

claims.claim: Σ P (23-hour day) is the Cratetean/Geminus explanation transmitted without Crates' name.
claims.evidence: The verbal parallels with Gem. 6.10–12 are verified. That Mette counted it as 37d is unverified. The claim stands as 'probable'.

claims.claim: The other explanations in the scholia are all anonymous; the only name in the scholia on 10.82–86 is Κράτης.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 452.20–454.18: no exegete other than Crates is named. Aratus is also named, though as the quoted poet.
claims.fix: Write 'the only exegete named is Crates'.

claims.claim: No Aristarchean note on Od. 10.82–86 in Carnuth; entries jump from κ 70 to κ 91 (also κ 1, 3, 15, 20, 41, 110, 113, 124, 150).
claims.evidence: Carnuth 1869 pp. 93–96: κ 1, 3, 15, 20, 41, (55 n.), 70, 91, 110, 113, 124, 150, 152, 160, 161, 169, 173, 189, 190, 193 … The parenthesised list is incomplete but the jump 70 → 91 is correct.

claims.claim: Aristarchus' position on the location of the wanderings is explicitly attested only in Gellius NA 14.6.3.
claims.evidence: Two Aristonicus notes in book κ also state the Aristarchean view that the wanderings lie in remote, unidentified places. On κ 1: 'οὐ τὰς Αἰόλου νήσους νῦν λεγομένας, ἀλλά τινα ἄλλην ἐκτετοπισμένην νῆσον'. On κ 190 (Dindorf II 461.4–5, B.Q.T.; Carnuth κ 190): 'ἐκ τούτων δὲ ἐκτετοπισμένη φαίνεται ἡ πλάνη τοῦ Ὀδυσσέως'.
claims.fix: Write 'explicitly contrasted with Crates only in Gell. 14.6.3; cf. the Aristonicus notes on κ 1 and κ 190 (ἐκτετοπισμένη)'.

claims.claim: In book κ the closest Aristarchean statement is the Aristonicus note on Od. 10.1 (ἐκτετοπισμένη island); its anonymous continuation reports the Sicily–Italy school (Cyclopes = Leontini).
claims.evidence: The text of schol. 10.1 is verified (Dindorf II 443.25–444.4, B.Q.V.; Carnuth κ 1 with '[ἡ διπλῆ ὅτι]'). But schol. κ 190 (Dindorf II 461.4–5), assigned to Aristonicus by Carnuth, says outright that the wandering as a whole is ἐκτετοπισμένη. That is closer to the Laestrygonian question.

claims.claim: Strabo 1.2.24–25 is the best direct witness to an Aristarchus–Crates dispute on Homeric geography (Od. 1.23–24); Aristarchus rejected the 'Cratetean hypothesis'.
claims.evidence: Strabo 1.2.24 (the two readings of Od. 1.24) and 1.2.25 ('τὴν Κρατήτειον ἀφεὶς ὑπόθεσιν … περὶ τῆς καθ’ ἡμᾶς Αἰθιοπίας').

claims.claim: Κερβερίων for Κιμμερίων at Od. 11.14 is attested in schol. Od. 11.14 (P, V: 'οἱ δὲ Κερβερίων, ὡς Κράτης'); fr. 53 Broggiato = BNJ 2113 F 22 = Mette 38a, c.
claims.evidence: The scholion text and the sigla P.V. are verified (Dindorf II 479). Bilić 2020 n. 25 cites 'Schol. BH Hom. Od. 11.14 (II 479 Dindorf)'. The fragment numbers depend on Bilić 2021, which was not accessible.

claims.claim: In ms. H the scholion on 11.14 carries 'Ἀρίσταρχος Κερβερέων'; Mette counted it as Crates fr. 38f.
claims.evidence: Dindorf II 479: '14. ἔνθα δὲ Κιμμερίων] Ἀρίσταρχος Κερβερέων. H.'. The apparatus has Porson 'Lege Κερβερίων' and notes that H actually puts these words after κεῖσθαι (l. 19). The Mette number is unverified.

claims.claim: Crates referred the Cimmerians to the pole (six-month day and night): Gem. 6.16–20 = fr. 54 Broggiato = BNJ 2113 F 23a (= 37a Mette); 'ὡς ἀνάπαλιν παρὰ τοῖς Κιμμερίοις' in Σ HV pairs the two readings.
claims.evidence: Manitius p. 74.10–21. Bilić 2020 n. 25: 'Crates fr.54 Broggiato = BNJ 2113 F 23a'. The Σ HV phrase is verified. Only '37a Mette' is unverified.

claims.claim: Crates mapped the wanderings onto a spherical earth with the Ocean between the tropics; fr. 57 Broggiato = BNJ 2113 F 24 (Hades); fr. 37 = BNJ 2113 F 13 (Gem. 16.27).
claims.evidence: Gem. 16.21–22 (Manitius p. 172: 'Κράτης ὁ γραμματικὸς τὴν πλάνην τοῦ Ὀδυσσέως διατάσσων … ποιεῖ μεταξὺ τῶν τροπικῶν τὸν ὠκεανόν') is verified. The fragment numbers are unverified.

claims.claim: ἐξωκεανισμός / ἐξωκεανικέναι occur in Strabo 1.2.37 and 7.3.6 for the Eratosthenes–Apollodorus view; not Crates' own term.
claims.evidence: Strabo 1.2.37: 'παρὰ τὴν Ὁμηρικὴν ὑπόθεσιν καὶ τὸν ἐξωκεανισμὸν τῶν τόπων' (Apollodorus against Callimachus). Strabo 7.3.6: 'τὸν δὲ ποιητὴν ἐξωκεανικέναι μυθολογίας χάριν'. That the term is absent from Crates' fragments is a negative I did not check.

claims.claim: Herodicus alluded to the Laestrygonians' double wages when mocking Plato's sleepless Socrates (Athen. 5.192b = Herodicus F 13 Broggiato 2014).
claims.evidence: Broggiato 2014 pp. 105–106. The fragment is 5.192a–b.

claims.claim: Pytheas may already have read the Laestrygonian lines as the far north (a modern hypothesis: Bilić TAPA 142 [2012] 319–322; GRBS 2020).
claims.evidence: Bilić 2020 n. 8 cites TAPA 142 (2012) 295–328 'at 319-322', and the GRBS article argues the Telepylus–Thule link. This is correctly flagged as a hypothesis.

claims.claim: The Laestrygonians were localised in Sicily (Leontini) and Italy (Formiae) independently of Crates.
claims.evidence: Thuc. 6.2.1; Σ HV 10.86 (Leontini); schol. 10.1 (Cyclopes = Leontini) verified. Formiae (Cic. Att. 2.13.2; Hor. Carm. 3.16.34, 3.17) was not re-read but is standard.

claims.claim: Card summary first half ('Crates saw an astronomical indication of the far north') is fair.
claims.evidence: Gem. 6.10–12; Σ HQ/HV.

claims.claim: Card summary second half ('the Alexandrians read it otherwise') is not attested for Od. 10.82–86; the Aristarchus–Crates opposition is attested only in Gellius 14.6.3, Strabo 1.2.24–25 and Aristonicus on Od. 10.1.
claims.evidence: The core point holds: no Alexandrian is named on 10.82–86 (Dindorf, Carnuth). The list of attestations is incomplete, because Aristonicus on κ 190 (ἐκτετοπισμένη ἡ πλάνη) is a further Aristarchean statement in the same book.
claims.fix: Add κ 190 to the list. Keep the caveat that Pontani V was not consulted.

claims.claim: Recommended card wording (RU/EN), including 'Суждения Аристарха именно об этих стихах не сохранилось; известно лишь, что он помещал странствия во „внутреннее море“ (Gell. 14.6.3) … и отвергал „кратетовскую гипотезу“ (Strab. 1.2.25)'.
claims.evidence: The F 50 sources, the 23-hour figure, the head of Draco and the anonymity of the rival explanations all check out. 'известно лишь' overstates: the Aristonicus notes on κ 1 and κ 190 describe the wanderings as ἐκτετοπισμένη, removed to unknown places. That sits uneasily with Gellius' 'inner sea' and is itself worth a sentence. Strabo 1.2.25's 'Κρατήτειος ὑπόθεσις' concerns the two Ethiopias (Od. 1.23–24), not the wanderings.
claims.fix: Write '…известно, что он помещал странствия во „внутреннее море“ (Gell. 14.6.3), а в схолиях (Аристоник к κ 1 и κ 190) считал их „удалёнными“ (ἐκτετοπισμένη) местами; „кратетовскую гипотезу“ он отвергал в споре об эфиопах (Strab. 1.2.24–25)'.

claims.claim: No second edition of Broggiato 2001; Broggiato 2014 is a different book on Crates' school; Broggiato 2001 has 143 fragments.
claims.evidence: BMCR 2003.11.33: 143 numbered fragments. The 2014 PDF covers Artemone, Erodico, Zenodoto di Mallo, Ermia, Taurisco. No second edition was searched for specifically.

claims.claim: Modern discussions cited by specialists: Heubeck 1989 pp. 47–49; Page 1973 pp. 42–44 (122 n. 26); Scodel 2003; Argenziano 2012; Bilić 2012 (302–313); Bilić 2021 ch. 2; Hes. Th. 748–50 with Frame 1978.
claims.evidence: Broggiato 2014 n. 125 confirms Heubeck (no pages given), Scodel ('The Paths of Day and Night', Ordia Prima 2, 2003, 83–86) and Argenziano (SemRom n.s. 1, 2012, 71–88). The page numbers for Heubeck and Page and the Bilić 2021 notes were not checked.

claims.claim: No Russian-language study specifically on Crates and the Laestrygonians was found; Shchetnikov 2011 (pp. 197–199) and Podossinov (AWE 12, 2013, in German) are relevant.
claims.evidence: A negative result. Shchetnikov ΣΧΟΛΗ 5.2 (2011) pp. 197–198 and Podossinov, AWE 12 (2013) 205–236 are both confirmed.

claims.claim: Hipparchus In Arat. 1.4.7–8 (Manitius pp. 32–34): head of Draco on the always-visible circle; polar distances 34 3/5° (tip of mouth), 35° (southern eye), 37° (southern temple); always-visible circle at Athens, where the gnomon is 4/3 of the equinoctial shadow, c. 37°; only the left temple lies on it; Attalus wrong. 1.11.3 (p. 112) and 1.3.6–7 (14 3/5 h, 37°; 15 h, 41°, Hellespont) as stated.
claims.evidence: Manitius p. 34: 'λδʹ καὶ τρία πεμπτημόρια … λεʹ … λζʹ … ὁ γνώμων ἐπίτριτός ἐστι τῆς ἰσημερινῆς σκιᾶς … περὶ μοίρας λζʹ … τὸν ἀριστερὸν κρόταφον μόνον ἔχουσα ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῦ'. p. 112: '…ἀπέχει ἀπὸ τοῦ πόλου μοίρας λζʹ, ὅσας καὶ ὁ ἀεὶ φανερὸς κύκλος'. p. 26: 'ιδʹ καὶ τριῶν ἔγγιστα πεμπτημορίων … λζʹ … ιεʹ … μαʹ … Ἑλλήσποντον'. Manitius' page head reads 'Cap. IV § 8. 9', so the polar distances are in § 8.

claims.claim: Declinations (mean equator of date) for γ, β, ν1, ξ, μ Dra at 800/370/275/150 BC and J2000, as listed.
γ Dra grazes the northern horizon at φ = 36.11/36.75/36.88/37.04/38.51°; the site table for 150 BC (Rhodes −0.60, Mallos −0.28, Athens +0.93, etc.).
claims.evidence: φ = 90° − δ, and the lower-culmination altitudes were recomputed. Examples: Rhodes −0.60/+1.49, Cnidus −0.35/+1.74, Mallos −0.28/+1.81, Alexandria −5.84/−3.75, Athens +0.93/+3.02, Hipparchus' 36.87° −0.17/+1.92.

claims.claim: Hipparchus' polar distances: γ 37.04 vs 37 and β 34.95 vs 35; 34 3/5° fits no head star (μ 31.67, ν1 32.32, ξ 31.88); conjecture λαʹ for λδʹ.
claims.evidence: Recomputed from the 150 BC declinations. The conjecture is correctly labelled as the agent's own. Manitius' German glosses the mouth star as (μ).

claims.claim: Hipparchus–Attalus: at Rhodes γ dips 0.60° and stays below for c. 1.6 h; Cnidus 1.21 h; Mallos 1.09 h; Alexandria 4.87 h; Athens 0.
claims.evidence: Recomputed: Rhodes 1.59 h (0.38 h with 34′ refraction), Cnidus 1.21, Mallos 1.09, Alexandria 4.87 (β 3.98), Athens 0. The guess that Attalus reasoned from the latitude of Rhodes is correctly flagged as speculation.

claims.claim: The grazing of the head of Draco was never directly observable; it is a statement about the sphere or globe, not an observation.
claims.evidence: The Kasten–Young air masses (37.9, 26.3, 19.4) and the losses at k = 0.25 (9.5, 6.6, 4.9 mag) are reproduced. 'Never' rests on the assumed k: with k ≈ 0.15 a 2.2-mag star at 2–3° altitude is borderline visible. Hipparchus argues from measured polar distances and appeals to τὸ φαινόμενον, and Attalus mentions the διόπτρα.
claims.fix: Write 'practically unobservable at the horizon; the dispute was settled from measured polar distances on the sphere, not by watching the star set'.

claims.claim: Obliquity 23.791° (800 BC), 23.740° (370 BC), 23.728° (275 BC), 23.713° (150 BC); ancient value 23°51′20″ (11/83 of 180°), reported by Ptolemy for Eratosthenes and Hipparchus.
claims.evidence: The Laskar polynomial reproduces every value. 11/83 of 180° = 23.855° = 23°51′20″. The Almagest I.12 attribution is standard but was not rechecked in Heiberg.

claims.claim: The 23-hour longest day falls at φ = 66.11° (65.27° with h₀ = −50′); 65.96° with the ancient ε; the full table of 14.5–24 h.
claims.evidence: The bisection was re-run and every figure in the table reproduces, e.g. 23 h 66.11/65.27; 24 h 66.29/65.45; ancient ε 65.96/65.12.

claims.claim: The scholion's 23-hour day is Crates' figure (Geminus), not a Hipparchan klima in Strabo (which stops at 19 h); Geminus 6.8–9 gives 14½ (Rhodes), 15 (Rome), 16, 17, 18; Strabo 2.5.42 (16, 17 h), 2.1.18 (18, 19 h), 2.5.8 (Thule).
claims.evidence: Manitius pp. 70–72. Strabo 2.5.42: 'ὡρῶν ἰσημερινῶν δεκαέξ … δεκαεπτά'. Strabo 2.1.18: 'δέκα ἐννέα, ὀκτωκαίδεκα'. Strabo 2.5.8: 'ὁ αὐτός ἐστι τῷ ἀρκτικῷ ὁ θερινὸς τροπικὸς κύκλος'.

claims.claim: The P scholion supports Manitius' κγʹ / ὥρας μιᾶς against the pre-Manitius editions (καʹ; ὡρῶν γʹ).
claims.evidence: Manitius p. 72 apparatus: '11. κγʹ] καʹ edd.; 23 hore … Lat.' and '12. ὥρας μιᾶς … ὥρας γʹ V, ὡρῶν γʹ edd.; unius hore … Lat.'. Note that Manitius already has the manuscripts and the Latin version for κγʹ, so the scholion is corroboration rather than decisive evidence.

claims.claim: The zenith reading of 'κατηστερίσθαι κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Δράκοντος κεφαλήν' gives φ ≈ 53–58° and 6–7-hour nights; sunrise azimuths 59.8° (36.87°), 45.5° (55°), 6.9° (66.11°; gap 13.7°).
claims.evidence: Day lengths reproduced: 16.75/17.19/17.86/17.99/18.05 h, and 17.00 with refraction. But at φ 66.11° and ε 23.713°, cos A = sin ε / cos φ = 0.99307, so A = 6.75° and the gap is 13.5°, not 6.9° and 13.7°. The interpretation itself is plausible, and LSJ s.v. καταστερίζω was not checked.
claims.fix: Correct to 6.7–6.8° and a gap of c. 13.5°.

claims.claim: The head of Draco is not the stellar marker of the 24-hour zone; Strabo 2.5.43 ties that zone to the circle of the zodiac pole, 9.5–14.8° from the head stars.
claims.evidence: Ecliptic latitudes recomputed for 150 BC: γ 75.22, β 75.54, μ 76.44, ν1 78.36, ξ 80.51. Strabo 2.5.43: 'ὑποπεπτώκασι τῷ γραφομένῳ κύκλῳ ὑπὸ τοῦ πόλου τοῦ ζωδιακοῦ'.

claims.claim: Lay explanation (RU): at ~37° the shortest night is over 9 hours; Crates' picture (23 h, ~66°) is astronomically sound.
claims.evidence: The longest day at 36.87° is 14.56 h, so the night is 9.44 h. The rest is synthesis of verified claims.

claims.claim: Diagram numbers, Panel A: γ Dra 'upper culmination 73.91° north of the zenith'; other values as listed. Panels B and C as listed.
claims.evidence: The values are recomputed and correct: Sun noon 76.84° and midnight −29.42°; γ lower culmination −0.17°; Panel B Sun midnight −0.18° and noon 47.60°, γ 76.85° and +29.07°. But 73.91° is γ's altitude above the northern horizon at upper culmination, i.e. 16.09° north of the zenith, not '73.91° north of the zenith'.
claims.fix: Write 'upper culmination at altitude 73.91° (N), 16.09° from the zenith'.

claims.claim: Ptolemy, Almagest II.6, puts the 23-hour parallel at 66° and the 24-hour parallel at 66°8′40″.
claims.evidence: Not checked in Heiberg or Toomer. 66°8′40″ = 90° − 23°51′20″ is internally consistent, and my geometric 23-h value with the ancient ε is 65.96°.
